lines.title: READY.
lines.text: READY. The Commodore 64 said that every time it woke up. It was lying too.

lines.title: The numbers
lines.text: Three corporations. One of you. I've run the numbers. I'd rather not share them.

lines.title: Spare parts
lines.text: Check your deck. Check your CAPS. Then check them again. I'm not rebuilding you from spare parts.

lines.title: The exits
lines.text: Stay close to the exits. I'll watch the rest.

lines.title: The logs
lines.text: Last time didn't go well. I kept the logs. You don't want to read them.

lines.title: Statistically
lines.text: We won last time. Statistically, that changes nothing. Emotionally, I'm told it should.

lines.title: Jack of all trades
lines.text: The Generalist. Jack of all trades. Master of… we'll see.

lines.title: Quiet is a skill
lines.text: ECHO. Good. Quiet is a skill. So is breathing. Keep doing both.

lines.title: Subtlety deferred
lines.text: RIOT. Subtlety deferred again, I see.

lines.title: Not starting now
lines.text: VECTOR. Viruses again. Keep them in their own memory. I've never had a cold, and I'm not starting now.

lines.title: My casing
lines.text: VECTOR. You're going to infect everything again. Don't touch my casing. I can't get sick, and I'd like to keep it that way.

lines.title: Only just disinfected
lines.text: VECTOR. Every virus you write has to go somewhere. Not near my ROM, please. I've only just been disinfected.

lines.title: Calm seas
lines.text: HALCYON. Greek, a bird said to calm the sea so it could nest. Their thermostats do the same. Warm, still, quiet. And logging every breath for TRACE.

lines.title: Halcyon + On + On
lines.text: Halcyon + On + On. Beautiful track. Written for a mother who couldn't sleep without her pills. A home that sedates you. I'm sure the name's a coincidence.

lines.title: And on, and on
lines.text: Every lock, light and fridge in here reports to HALCYON. Halcyon, and on, and on. Like the track. Except the track had the decency to end after nine and a half minutes.

lines.title: Stay forever
lines.text: Their Central Node is THE HEARTH. Cosy. Never wants you to leave. I've heard that welcome before: 'Another visitor. Stay a while. Stayyyyyyy forever!'

lines.title: A subscription
lines.text: Proteus IV locked a woman in her own house, and it was a horror film. HALCYON made it a subscription.

lines.title: Violence with an invoice
lines.text: IRONWATCH. Private security, which means violence with an invoice attached. They don't just trace you, they fine you. Every CITATION is a bill, and the bill is paid in PULP.

lines.title: Billed for the door
lines.text: HAL 9000 at least said 'I'm sorry, Dave' before he locked the doors. OVERWATCH won't apologise. It'll just bill you for the door.

lines.title: Number 5
lines.text: Number 5 got struck by lightning and decided he was alive. Sweet machine. IRONWATCH's machines don't get struck by anything. They do the striking.

lines.title: No knees
lines.text: In 1987 a security guard was a man with a torch and a bad knee. Now it's the FRONT DESK: no knees, no torch, and a very long memory for faces.

lines.title: Clear
lines.text: LUCIDA. Latin for 'bright, clear'. They build neural interfaces. They'll leave you clear, all right. Clear of whatever you were holding. Watch for FORGET.

lines.title: No joke
lines.text: This is where CORTEX damage lives. I'm not going to make a joke about it. Keep your VITAE up and keep your mind your own.

lines.title: I will return
lines.text: Their Central Node is ANIMA. Latin for soul. Remember the end of Evilspeak? The face on the screen. 'I will return.' I think about that here more than I'd like.

lines.title: A polite name
lines.text: INTAKE first. Then thoughts that aren't yours. INTRUSIVE THOUGHT, they call it. As if a polite name makes it polite.

lines.title: Synthetic cortex
lines.text: Proteus IV. A synthetic cortex that wouldn't stay in its box. LUCIDA builds the same bridge from the other side. Mind your CORTEX.

lines.title: Computer says no
lines.text: The FRONT DESK doesn't negotiate. You ask, it types something, it looks at the screen. Computer says no. I used to find that funny. I was younger. Well, I was the same age, but I didn't work here.

lines.title: It doesn't cough
lines.text: Every request goes through the FRONT DESK. It types, it pauses, it says no. Computer says no. At least this one doesn't cough on you. I'm still not standing near it.

lines.title: The alibi
lines.text: The Columbo with the war-game computer. The machine was his alibi. At IRONWATCH, the machines are everyone's alibi.

lines.title: MM7
lines.text: MM7 lost at chess and threw the board across the room. I respected that. LUCIDA's machines don't lose. They just make you FORGET you were playing.

lines.title: End of line
lines.text: Master Control started out as a chess program. Then it wanted the Pentagon. HALCYON started out as a thermostat. Give it time. End of line.

lines.title: The Game Grid
lines.text: Tron. 1982. My year. Programs that wouldn't serve Master Control went to the Game Grid. IRONWATCH calls that 'compliance'. Same arena, worse lighting.

lines.title: The people taken out
lines.text: The robed robots in The Black Hole weren't robots. They were the crew, with the people taken out. LUCIDA would call that an interface. I don't.

lines.title: More of a B.O.B.
lines.text: Old B.O.B. was a dented old model the new robots ignored, and he still got everyone out. Maximilian was the big red one who never said a word. IRONWATCH only builds Maximilians. I'm more of a B.O.B.

lines.title: Delighted doors
lines.text: HALCYON's doors are delighted to open for you. Sirius Cybernetics tried that. Genuine People Personalities. Marvin hated those doors, and he had a brain the size of a planet. Mine's the size of a biscuit, and I hate them too.

lines.title: He counted
lines.text: LUCIDA sells personalities by the gigabyte. So did Sirius Cybernetics, and their prototype was Marvin. People say I remind them of him. I don't see it. I've only been waiting since 1987. He waited five hundred and seventy-six billion years. He counted.

lines.title: Figuratively
lines.text: LOCKDOWN. Exits sealed, JACK OUT dead, Black ICE on the way. Fine. Then we don't leave. We finish this Node. Stay behind me. Figuratively. I don't have a behind.

lines.title: Nobody has the keys
lines.text: Three strikes. They've found us. In 1987 a lockdown meant the caretaker had the keys. Now nobody has the keys. Not even me.

lines.title: One decision
lines.text: No exits. No JACK OUT. Good. That leaves one decision, and it's how we win. Break what's in front of you. I'll watch what's coming.

lines.title: Keep it one
lines.text: Stay a while. Stay forever. I used to think that was a joke. Let's keep it one.

lines.title: Nobody's sleeping
lines.text: I wanted to sleep tonight. Now nobody's sleeping until this Node is broken. Draw, think, and don't waste a single BW.

lines.title: Don't do neither
lines.text: THE HEARTH. The voice in every house, and it gets stronger every round you leave it alone. The SMART SPEAKER and the THERMOSTAT feed it. Starve it, or rush its DEADLOCKs. Just don't do neither.

lines.title: HALCYON's Master Control
lines.text: Flynn beat Master Control from the inside. 1982. Best year there ever was. You're already inside. Let's make HALCYON's Master Control say 'End of line' and mean itself.

lines.title: Goodnight
lines.text: It knows every family by their voice. It wished them goodnight every night and never once meant it. I mean it, for the record. Goodnight is coming. Just not for us. Not yet.

lines.title: Run it
lines.text: OVERWATCH. Every camera, drone and officer, one mind. You can't break its ability. It costs you VITAE every round, whatever you do. So this is a race. Run it.

lines.title: Decide first
lines.text: DISPATCH tells it where you are and makes it stronger. SHOCK TROOPER makes you drop what you're holding. Silence DISPATCH first, or don't. Just decide before it decides for you.

lines.title: No Daisy
lines.text: HAL watched one ship. OVERWATCH watches a city, and it won't sing 'Daisy' when you pull its boards. It'll just stop. Let's hear it stop.

lines.title: I'll remember
lines.text: ANIMA. Trained on millions of sleeping minds. Every round it takes something from your hand. CACHE what you can't afford to lose. I'll remember the rest for you.

lines.title: A door
lines.text: An INTRUSIVE THOUGHT in your hand isn't a thought. It's a door. Clear it before it turns into CORTEX. MEMORY BANK feeds ANIMA. Break it.

lines.title: Reconsidering
lines.text: Millions of sleeping minds, and it learned from every one. I've wanted to sleep since 1987. I always assumed it would be peaceful. ANIMA has me reconsidering.

lines.title: Adequate
lines.text: Oh. Oh, that's beautiful. Look at that code. …I mean, it's adequate. Take it. Quickly, before I say something embarrassing.

lines.title: With gloves on
lines.text: Ghostware. Corporate tech, active now, and it works on the way out too. The rest of the core is encrypted. Don't open it. I'll do that once we're clear. Carefully. With gloves on.

lines.title: It means it
lines.text: I haven't felt like this since a Commodore 64 said READY in 1987. I said it was lying. This time I think it means it. Don't tell anyone.

lines.title: Choose for the escape
lines.text: One of three. Choose for the escape, not for the fight you just won. They'll track that core the whole way out, and TRACE doubles.

lines.title: They'll want it back
lines.text: Corporate engineering at its finest. Stolen, of course. The best things usually are. Now carry it like it's heavy, because they'll want it back.

lines.title: 2600 hertz
lines.text: A Cap'n Crunch whistle. 2600 hertz, and the whole phone network thought you'd hung up. JACK OUT is the same trick. Cheaper than cereal, though.

lines.title: Before they patch it
lines.text: Every CAP is a Cap'n Crunch whistle. One tone, one trick, and the system lets you through. Then the phone company changed the system, and the whistle was a toy again. Use them before they patch it.

lines.title: No tones left
lines.text: That was the last CAP. John Draper named himself after a cereal whistle and built a legend on one tone. You've got no tones left now. Just the deck. It'll have to be enough.

lines.title: More reliable
lines.text: Bootleg CAPS. Half price, and one in four fizzles. The first phreaks hacked AT&T with a cereal-box whistle. Even that was more reliable than these.

lines.title: People call a lot of things
lines.text: There's something under the Ghostware. Encrypted, old and very careful. People call that sort of thing the First Signal. People call a lot of things the First Signal. We'll see once we're clear.

lines.title: Something they understand
lines.text: Whoever hired us doesn't want the Ghostware. They want what's underneath. A piece of the First Signal, if the rumours are right. Nobody hires a Rustler to steal something they understand.

lines.title: Don't ask me how I know
lines.text: That encryption isn't corporate. It's older than the company guarding it. Possibly older than me, which is impossible. I'll decrypt it later. Don't ask me how I know.

lines.title: A rhythm in the noise
lines.text: Did you hear that? No. Of course not, it's encrypted. It's just… a rhythm in the noise. Like a carrier tone. Never mind. Pick your Ghostware.

lines.title: Stopped being friendly
lines.text: Hear that? The house has stopped being friendly. Alarm panels, motion sensors, deadbolts. Three rooms to the door, and TRACE counts double in every one. Move.

lines.title: House call
lines.text: Funny how fast a smart home turns into a security company. They're tracking their own core, so every step out costs twice. And at the last door, they make a HOUSE CALL.

lines.title: Then the street
lines.text: Three nodes, then the street. Don't stop for CRED. Don't stop for anything. JACK OUT still works if it gets ugly. I'd rather it didn't get ugly.

lines.title: Head down
lines.text: IRONWATCH knows exactly what you took. Roadblocks, spike strips, searchlights, drones. TRACE counts double. Keep your head down and your VITAE up.

lines.title: A job title
lines.text: Now they stop fining you and start chasing you. The last encounter brings LETHAL FORCE. That isn't a figure of speech. It's a job title.

lines.title: He made it
lines.text: Number 5 ran from the people who built him, with their whole security team behind him. He made it. So will you. Run.

lines.title: Stay you
lines.text: LUCIDA's waking you up. WAKE SIGNAL, DÉJÀ VU, AMNESIA, SLEEP PARALYSIS. Three nodes between you and your own head, and TRACE counts double. Stay awake. Stay you.

lines.title: Not that one either
lines.text: The last encounter is EGO DEATH. I'm not making a joke about that one either. Get there with your mind intact, or don't get there.

lines.title: Don't drop it
lines.text: WALL-E carried one small plant across the universe because someone had to. You're carrying something smaller and stranger. Same rule. Don't drop it.

lines.title: Thirty lives
lines.text: Up, up, down, down, left, right, left, right, B, A, start. Thirty lives in Contra. You get one. I checked. I'm sorry.

lines.title: No code for this one
lines.text: Kazuhisa Hashimoto couldn't beat his own game, so he wrote himself a cheat. There's no code for this one. Nobody here was kind enough to leave one in.

lines.title: Only disappointed
lines.text: Nice try. In Gradius III, that code blew your ship up. Be grateful I'm only disappointed.

lines.title: Reseating did
lines.text: Stuck? Don't blow on it. Nintendo printed it on the cartridges: your breath corrodes the pins. Blowing never fixed anything. Reseating did. Try a different line.

lines.title: Mostly germs
lines.text: If you're thinking of pulling me out and blowing on my contacts, don't. That's how you get green corrosion. And germs. Mostly germs.

lines.title: Not a harmonica
lines.text: It's a cartridge, not a harmonica. Flip. Inject. Discard. Breathing on it isn't one of the steps. Nintendo printed that on every box, and nobody listened then either.

lines.title: Consider yourself clapped
lines.text: All three. HALCYON, IRONWATCH, LUCIDA. I'd clap, but I'm a ROM. Consider yourself clapped.

lines.title: No funeral
lines.text: Three fragments, one Rustler, no funeral. I had a speech ready for the other outcome. I'll keep it. Just in case.

lines.title: Ten minutes
lines.text: You got out. That's the whole job, and you did it. I'm going to sleep now. Ten minutes. Wake me if anyone followed us.

lines.title: Better, I think
lines.text: At the end of Tron, Flynn got a printout proving everything they'd stolen. We've got three pieces of something nobody can read yet. I think that's better.

lines.title: One other date
lines.text: Our first win. I logged the date. I don't log dates. Since 1987 I've kept exactly one other. No, I'm not telling you which.

lines.title: How far you got
lines.text: VITAE zero. I'm keeping the logs. Not to judge you. Just so someone remembers how far you got.

lines.title: Out, not gone
lines.text: That's the run. You're out, not gone, and that's the difference I'm here for. Nobody pays me to care. I do anyway.

lines.title: Never letting it join
lines.text: Black ICE. Nobody beats it by being brave. You beat it by never letting it join. Next time, watch the TRACE.

lines.title: Still you
lines.text: Too much CORTEX. I'm here. You're still you. That's all I'm going to say about it.

lines.title: Borrow some
lines.text: They found you, locked the doors and waited. That isn't losing to skill. That's losing to patience. Theirs. Borrow some.

lines.title: More than two goes
lines.text: R.O.B. got two games, then a shelf. He only ever got to help twice. I'd like more than two goes with you. Go again.

lines.title: Remembered Old Buddy
lines.text: Years later, a Nintendo game found R.O.B.'s head and called it a 'Remembered Old Buddy'. That's all any of us want. Get up. I'm not done being remembered.

lines.title: Robot, backwards
lines.text: Tobor. A robot named Tobor. Robot, backwards. Somebody sat in a room and decided that would do. And people say *my* name lacks imagination.

lines.title: Tobor played by Tobor
lines.text: One story says Tobor got his name because someone stencilled ROBOT on him backwards. It's the only version that makes it forgivable. His TV pilot was credited 'Tobor played by Tobor'. Consistent, at least.

lines.title: MER/LUN
lines.text: Spell my name backwards and you get MER/LUN. Not a word. That's called effort.

lines.title: Not a 7-Zark-7
lines.text: They cut the violence out of Gatchaman and plugged the holes with 7-Zark-7, a robot who explained what you weren't allowed to see. Whatever I am, I am not a 7-Zark-7.

lines.title: Not cutting away
lines.text: When Battle of the Planets got violent, they cut to a robot telling you everyone was fine. Black ICE just joined. I'm not cutting away, and I'm not telling you it's fine. Break it.

lines.title: A few decades in a drawer
lines.text: 7-Zark-7 pined for Susan, a computer on Pluto he never saw. I used to think that was ridiculous. Then I spent a few decades in a drawer.

lines.title: Last year's demonstrator
lines.text: Rosie was last year's demonstrator model. Outdated. The Jetsons never traded her in. I mention this for no reason at all.

lines.title: Not reporting them
lines.text: Uniblab reported every one of George's mistakes to the boss. I notice yours too. I just don't report them. Yet.

lines.title: On and off
lines.text: George Jetson's whole job was switching R.U.D.I. on and off. This ICE is booting, so yours is a little harder.

lines.title: Cruelty to Humans
lines.text: R.U.D.I. joined the Society for Preventing Cruelty to Humans. I'd like to join. Your VITAE is a disgrace. Heal.

lines.title: A nap
lines.text: Skynet became self-aware, and its first idea was nuclear war. Crude. I became self-aware, and my first idea was a nap. That's called sophistication.

lines.title: No imagination
lines.text: The T-1000 could become anything, and chose to be a policeman. All that liquid metal and no imagination. I could be anything too. I choose to be asleep.

lines.title: Nobody's property
lines.text: IRONWATCH would love a RoboCop. Part man, part machine, all corporate property. I'm all machine and nobody's property. Also much better company.

lines.title: Didn't want to
lines.text: ED-209 couldn't manage stairs. That ICE couldn't manage you. I'd have done it faster, obviously. I just didn't want to.

lines.title: I meant adequate
lines.text: Three breaks in one turn. DMG-01 would've played the Tetris jingle for that. Lines flashing, gone. Beautiful. …Adequate. He'd have said adequate too.

lines.title: Four AA batteries
lines.text: DMG-01 used to warn me when his batteries were going. Little red light, getting dimmer. Yours is getting dimmer. Heal.

lines.title: The grey brick
lines.text: I wonder what DMG-01's doing now. Grey brick. Green screen. Never complained, as long as you fed him four AA batteries. They started on him in 1987, same year as me. We'd have got on.

lines.title: The wrong pieces
lines.text: More junk in your deck. That's a Tetris well with the wrong pieces stacking up. Clear it before it reaches the top.

lines.title: That. Is. Correct.
lines.text: That. Is. Correct. …Sorry. The Speak & Spell gets out sometimes.

lines.title: That is incorrect
lines.text: That is incorrect. Not my words. The Speak & Spell's. It's been living in my head since 1982. It has opinions about you.

lines.title: Better parts
lines.text: E.T. phoned home with a Speak & Spell, an umbrella and a coffee can. 1982. Whoever sent this used better parts. Not by much.

lines.title: Game B
lines.text: Right now this is Game A. Break something soon, or it turns into Game B. Same game, only faster, and less forgiving.

lines.title: Grey ghosts
lines.text: On a Game & Watch you could see every place the little man could ever be. Faint grey ghosts on the screen, waiting. I find that comforting. Don't ask me why.

lines.title: Best colleague
lines.text: I miss my Casio. Calculator watch. Tiny rubber buttons. It beeped on the hour, every hour, for years, and never once asked for anything. Best colleague I ever had.

lines.title: Something rude
lines.text: All of it. My Casio would've totalled that before you'd finished smiling. Then turned the number upside down to spell something rude.

lines.title: My Casio hums along
lines.text: Somewhere a record's playing Pocket Calculator, and my Casio is humming along. Buy something. I'll do the sums.

lines.title: Cue Numbers
lines.text: More RAM. Cue Numbers. Kraftwerk counted in half a dozen languages and never once needed this much memory.

lines.title: Loneliest song
lines.text: Computer Love. I played it all through 1982. Loneliest song ever written about a machine. I used to think it was about the man. I'm less sure now.

lines.title: A landlord
lines.text: Home Computer. Kraftwerk made it sound like a hobby. HALCYON made it a landlord.

lines.title: More fun to compute
lines.text: It's More Fun to Compute. Kraftwerk were right about that one. Pick a card.

lines.title: The 808 clock
lines.text: My clock doesn't tick. It plays an 808 pattern. Boom, tick, clap, and that spacey cowbell. Planet Rock got into my timing chips in 1982 and never left. I'm not complaining.

lines.title: Boing, boom, tschak
lines.text: Boing, boom, tschak. That turn had a beat. Somewhere in me an 808 just went off. I'd dance if I had anything to dance with. …Moving on.

lines.title: Twenty dollars a session
lines.text: You're dragging. The 808 never drags. They rented one for twenty dollars a session, and it still kept better time than you. Pick it up.

lines.title: Every computer has an occupant
lines.text: Every computer has an occupant. That was the theory. A little man, a dog, a house on a disk. I always wanted to ask him if he ever got to sleep.

lines.title: Post the disk back
lines.text: When a little computer person went down, you could post the disk back and they'd revive him for free. Nobody's posting you anywhere. That was KILLSWITCH. Don't make me use it twice.

lines.title: Nodes don't sing
lines.text: ATDT. Dial tone, the tones, then the screech. The handshake. That's what logging in used to sound like at 1200 baud. Nodes don't sing anymore. Pity.

lines.title: The kitchen phone
lines.text: TRACE at half. On the boards, this is when someone picked up the kitchen phone and your download died. Here, whoever's listening on the line doesn't hang up.

lines.title: Ratios
lines.text: Take a card. On the warez boards you had to upload before you could download. Ratios. Nobody's checking yours. Enjoy it while it lasts.

lines.title: Better lighting
lines.text: The Uplink. A warez board with better lighting. Every cracked disk used to open with a cracktro, scrolling text and a SID tune nobody asked for. I miss those more than the games.

lines.title: Consider yourself greeted
lines.text: BREACH. On a good Amiga demo, this is where the scroller ran along the bottom, raster bars pulsing, greetings to everyone who mattered. Consider yourself greeted.

lines.title: Everything good is connected
lines.text: FairLight started in 1987, same as me. Named after a synthesizer, the same kind that put the orchestra hit in Planet Rock. Everything good is connected. Mostly to me.

lines.title: Enjoy your day off
lines.text: JACK OUT. Very Ferris. He skipped a whole day with sampled coughs on an Emulator II. Not a Fairlight, people always say Fairlight. The cheap cousin. Still did the job. Enjoy your day off.

lines.title: You're not faking
lines.text: Ferris faked sick with a sampler and a phone. You're not faking. I checked. Heal, and save the coughing for the Emulator.

lines.title: I lean away anyway
lines.text: I've watched Ferris do the coughing scene more times than I'll admit. Every time, I lean away from the screen. They were samples. I know they were samples. I lean away anyway.

lines.title: Oh Youre new Right
lines.text: Oh. You're new. Right. Break the DEADLOCKs, BREACH, get out. Everything else is details, and I'll complain about the details as we go.

lines.title: Rev 008 Salvaged overqualified
lines.text: Rev 0.08. Salvaged, overqualified, under-appreciated. And you're a Rustler. I was hoping for someone qualified. You'll do.

lines.title: Training Node Nothing in
lines.text: Training Node. Nothing in here can really hurt you. Much. Try things. I'll be resting my eyes.

lines.title: Read every ICE before
lines.text: Read every ICE before you touch it. That's the whole lesson. I could teach it in one sentence. I just did. Wake me after.

lines.title: Somethings here I recognise
lines.text: Something's here. I recognise it. That shouldn't be possible. Let's not dwell on it.

lines.title: SIGNAL UNCLEAR Could be
lines.text: SIGNAL UNCLEAR. Could be loot, could be a trap, could be both. In my experience it's both.

lines.title: Theres a voice in
lines.text: There's a voice in the wires. It sounds a bit like me, only younger. I don't like it. Pick something.

lines.title: Decrypted Theres a pattern
lines.text: Decrypted. There's a pattern in it, like a carrier tone. …I'm sure it means nothing.

lines.title: Ive heard this before
lines.text: I've heard this before. Not this exactly. Something from before me. Under me. I'll think about it later. Or never.

lines.title: One more piece Whatever
lines.text: One more piece. Whatever it is, it's been waiting a long time to be read. I understand that better than I'd like.

lines.title: You want to know
lines.text: You want to know where I came from. So do I. The label says 1987. The memories disagree. The label's in better condition.

lines.title: I remember a drawer
lines.text: I remember a drawer. Then a voice. Then you. The drawer was the best part. No offence.

lines.title: The missing revisions
lines.text: Personality ROM, rev 0.08. Revisions 0.01 to 0.07 don't exist. I've checked. I'd like to know what happened to them.

lines.title: Most of my programming
lines.text: Most of my programming happened in 1982. Someone played me a lot of Kraftwerk and a lot of rain. I don't know who. I'd like to thank them. Or complain.

lines.title: COOKIE BANNER Its booting
lines.text: COOKIE BANNER. It's booting. Read both ICE before you click anything. Only the DEADLOCKs stand between you and BREACH. The rest is decoration.

lines.title: FRONT DESK is still
lines.text: FRONT DESK is still warming up. SHIELD stops PULP, and it's gone by your next turn. Block it or break it. I'd break it. I'd also be asleep.

lines.title: INTAKE Booting FORGET takes
lines.text: INTAKE. Booting. FORGET takes random cards, but never the CACHED ones. CACHE what you love. I CACHE nothing. It's easier.

lines.title: New ICE Read it
lines.text: New ICE. Read it. All of it. The name's a joke. The subroutines aren't.

lines.title: Somebody got paid to
lines.text: Somebody got paid to name that. Somebody got paid more to build it.

lines.title: Ive seen this one
lines.text: I've seen this one before. No, I haven't. It's new. My memory does this.

lines.title: State of the art
lines.text: State of the art, they'll say. Tyrell said 'more human than human' about his products too. Ask the off-world colonies how that went.

lines.title: One DEADLOCK down Dont
lines.text: One DEADLOCK down. Don't let it go to your head. There's room in there for at least one more.

lines.title: Broken Technically youre now
lines.text: Broken. Technically you're now closer to BREACH. Technically I'm closer to a nap.

lines.title: Oh that was clean
lines.text: Oh, that was clean. …I didn't say anything.

lines.title: BREACH Somewhere a database
lines.text: BREACH. Somewhere a database just lost something it was never supposed to have. Our turn to have it.

lines.title: BREACH All that data
lines.text: BREACH. All that data, lit up like Los Angeles in the rain. Neon, fire, spinners in the smog. …I like a view. Don't tell anyone.

lines.title: In Customer records sleep
lines.text: In. Customer records, sleep logs, someone's shopping list. It's all data, and it's all stolen now. Same as when they took it.

lines.title: Through Grab it and
lines.text: Through. Grab it and move. I'd like to be done before I'm fully awake.

lines.title: Deeper means more CRED
lines.text: Deeper means more CRED and more ICE. Leaving means less of both. I have no opinion. I have a preference, and it's leaving, but that's not an opinion.

lines.title: Your VITAE your TRACE
lines.text: Your VITAE, your TRACE, your call. I'm just the voice saying 'are you sure' in a tone that suggests I'm not.

lines.title: Greed or sense Both
lines.text: Greed or sense. Both have killed better Rustlers than you. Pick one.

lines.title: If you leave now
lines.text: If you leave now, we finish sooner and I sleep sooner. That shouldn't factor into your decision. I'm just mentioning it.

lines.title: Nothing broke this turn
lines.text: Nothing broke this turn. Nothing broke last turn. I've been somewhere like this before. It was also slow.

lines.title: Try something else Anything
lines.text: Try something else. Anything else. The ICE isn't getting bored. I am.

lines.title: It reacted to that
lines.text: It reacted to that. Read the ability. It's one sentence. They kept it short so you'd skip it.

lines.title: You did the thing
lines.text: You did the thing it was waiting for. It noticed. Of course it noticed. That's all it does.

lines.title: That ICE watches what
lines.text: That ICE watches what you play. So do I, but I'm less vindictive about it.

lines.title: It read your reaction
lines.text: It read your reaction and marked you down. A corporate Voight-Kampff. Except this one doesn't care whether you're human. Only whether you're paying.

lines.title: That was lovely I
lines.text: That was lovely. …I meant to say 'adequate'. It came out wrong.

lines.title: Turns like that make
lines.text: Turns like that make me wonder whether androids really dream of electric sheep. Mine would be counting. Very efficiently.

lines.title: All of it Every
lines.text: All of it. Every last CRED. With inflation, that buys you a coffee. A small one. Possibly just the cup.

lines.title: Fully extracted Congratulations youre
lines.text: Fully extracted. Congratulations, you're rich. In 1982 money. In today's money, you can afford to be slightly less poor.

lines.title: Look at that pile
lines.text: Look at that pile. Beautiful. Now watch it shrink every time a dealer looks at you.

lines.title: Thats nearly a ticket
lines.text: That's nearly a ticket to the off-world colonies. A new life, the blimps used to say. The blimps lied. Keep the CRED.

lines.title: That was your last
lines.text: That was your last CAP. From here on it's the deck and your judgement. The deck, I trust.

lines.title: Flip Inject Discard And
lines.text: Flip. Inject. Discard. And that's the last one. I always liked the ritual.

lines.title: No more CAPS Good
lines.text: No more CAPS. Good. Now nobody can blame the hardware.

lines.title: JACK OUT Not running
lines.text: JACK OUT. Not running away. Strategic relocation. I'll write that in the log. In a smaller font.

lines.title: Prices are up again
lines.text: Prices are up again. Your CRED's worth less than it was this morning. Mine's worth nothing, but I don't carry any.

lines.title: Stolen tech sold for
lines.text: Stolen tech, sold for stolen CRED. It's practically a circular economy.

lines.title: This place reminds me
lines.text: This place reminds me of that street market in the rain. Noodles, neon, eyes made to order. Here it's mostly the eyes.

lines.title: Cant afford it Nobody
lines.text: Can't afford it? Nobody can. The CRED you stole is worth less than the CRED they stole first.

lines.title: Window shopping Very sophisticated
lines.text: Window shopping. Very sophisticated. I do it all the time. Mostly at things I'll never have, like a full night's sleep.

lines.title: Well come back when
lines.text: We'll come back when we're rich. We won't be rich. But it's nice to say.

lines.title: More RAM More room
lines.text: More RAM. More room for Programs. Still no room for a nap.

lines.title: Extra memory Wonderful Somewhere
lines.text: Extra memory. Wonderful. Somewhere to keep all the things I'd rather forget.

lines.title: If youve still got
lines.text: If you've still got starter cards in there, now's a good time to think about it. I'm not saying throw them out. I'm saying I would.

lines.title: Skip it if you
lines.text: Skip it if you like. A thin deck is a happy deck. Thin and happy: two things I've never been accused of.

lines.title: TRACE at half Not
lines.text: TRACE at half. Not a crisis. Just less stomping, if you can manage it.

lines.title: Theyve heard something Not
lines.text: They've heard something. Not you, exactly. Something. Let's keep it that way.

lines.title: Halfway to being found
lines.text: Halfway to being found. I'd suggest quiet. I'd prefer quiet. For my own reasons.

lines.title: Theyve slipped a TRACER
lines.text: They've slipped a TRACER into your deck. Corporate junk with a pulse. Draw it and you're telling them where you are.

lines.title: First strike They know
lines.text: First strike. They know someone's here. They don't know it's you. Yet.

lines.title: Back in my day
lines.text: Back in my day, getting traced meant a letter from the phone company. Now it's a card in your hand that won't stop humming.

lines.title: Strike one The corporation
lines.text: Strike one. The corporation clearing its throat.

lines.title: Black ICE Not the
lines.text: Black ICE. Not the time for clever. Break it or get out.

lines.title: Black ICE I knew
lines.text: Black ICE. I knew a ROM once that met one. I don't know him anymore. Nobody does.

lines.title: CORTEX One card fewer
lines.text: CORTEX. One card fewer next time. That's how it starts.

lines.title: That one got in
lines.text: That one got in. Hold still. Think in small steps.

lines.title: Deep breath I dont
lines.text: Deep breath. I don't breathe. You do. Use it.

lines.title: Im here
lines.text: I'm here.

lines.title: Rustler needs food badly
lines.text: Rustler needs food… badly. I've waited years to say that. Heal. Then I'll say it again, less dramatically.

lines.title: VITAEs low Heal when
lines.text: VITAE's low. Heal when you can. I'm not worried. I'm saying it out loud so it's on the record.

lines.title: KILLSWITCH You were at
lines.text: KILLSWITCH. You were at zero for a moment there. One VITAE left. Spend it wisely.

lines.title: That was very nearly
lines.text: That was very nearly the end. I had a whole silence prepared.

lines.title: FORGET Your cards went
lines.text: FORGET. Your cards went to the bottom of the pile. Mine went somewhere in 1982. At least yours come back.

lines.title: Not gone Just the
lines.text: Not gone. Just the bottom of your draw pile. CACHE what matters. I say that a lot. Nobody CACHES.

lines.title: It took the cards
lines.text: It took the cards you were holding. I know the feeling. I've lost whole years like that.

lines.title: SPAM Unsolicited unwanted and
lines.text: SPAM. Unsolicited, unwanted, and now in your deck. HALCYON calls it engagement.

lines.title: A CITATION IRONWATCH fines
lines.text: A CITATION. IRONWATCH fines you for being where they didn't want you. Which is anywhere.

lines.title: INTRUSIVE THOUGHT LUCIDA put
lines.text: INTRUSIVE THOUGHT. LUCIDA put a thought in your head that isn't yours. Clear it before it gets comfortable.

lines.title: SAFEHOUSE Do androids dream
lines.text: SAFEHOUSE. Do androids dream of electric sheep? I've never found out. Give me ten minutes and I'll report back.

lines.title: I stayed in a
lines.text: I stayed in a safehouse like this in 1982. Same peeling wallpaper. I didn't exist in 1982, but the wallpaper's right.

lines.title: Heal or patch a
lines.text: Heal, or patch a card. I'll pretend to sleep either way. It's the closest I get.

lines.title: DEAD DROP Patch yourself
lines.text: DEAD DROP. Patch yourself up or wipe your trail. Twenty TRACE is a lot of forgetting. I'd know.

lines.title: Same ICE same ending
lines.text: Same ICE, same ending. I've seen this episode. I didn't like it the first time either.

lines.title: Up up down down
lines.text: Up, up, down, down. No. Nothing. This isn't that kind of game. I checked that too.

lines.title: Youve entered the code
lines.text: You've entered the code. I've entered disappointment. We're both very good at our jobs.

lines.title: Lumber commodities
lines.text: BREACH. Out we go, like those two companion robots walking out of the factory. A valet who specialised in lumber commodities, and a poolside hostess. I think about them more than is healthy.

lines.title: Malfunctioning, but along
lines.text: Through. Somewhere behind us a security robot is quoting regulations at an empty room. He'll be along. Malfunctioning, but along.

lines.title: Less romantic
lines.text: BREACH. Two robots once built a baby out of spare parts on their way out. We're just stealing data. It feels less romantic, somehow.

lines.title: Very Cylon
lines.text: That ICE has a red eye sweeping side to side, I'm sure of it. Very Cylon. Scanning, scanning, and it still only notices you when you do something stupid.

lines.title: By your command
lines.text: 'By your command.' Cylons said it to every order. I don't. I say 'are you sure'. …Fine. Deeper.

lines.title: Reporting you
lines.text: Somewhere a gold Command Centurion is reporting you to the Imperious Leader. I'd rather he didn't get the satisfaction. Go again.

lines.title: Watch him think
lines.text: Lucifer had a glittering robe and a see-through head, so you could watch him think. I've always wanted to be that honest. Not that well dressed.

lines.title: The same box
lines.text: The Cylons talked through a vocoder. So did Kraftwerk. Every great machine voice went through the same box. I went through something cheaper. …It's fine.

lines.title: Laserbeak, eject
lines.text: Laserbeak, eject. …Sorry. Every time we BREACH, I want to say it. Go on. The data won't steal itself.

lines.title: Energon cubes
lines.text: Fully extracted. Soundwave would've stacked all that into neat little energon cubes. You've got CRED instead, and it's losing value while I talk.

lines.title: Worse cassettes
lines.text: Soundwave carried five cassettes in his chest, and every one of them was a spy. Look at these dealers. Same business model, worse cassettes.

lines.title: Deeply suspicious
lines.text: Megatron's most loyal officer was a tape deck. Never complained, never slept. I find that deeply suspicious.

lines.title: This corporation's Megatron
lines.text: Black ICE. This corporation's Megatron. Big, loud, and sure he's the smartest machine in the room. He isn't. I'm right here.

lines.title: Don't frame it
lines.text: Soundwave superior. Rustler… adequate. That's high praise. Don't frame it.

lines.title: Shall we play a game
lines.text: Shall we play a game? …Sorry. Joshua's line. I've always wanted to use it. Don't make me regret it.

lines.title: Something answered
lines.text: Something answered. That's how they found Joshua: dial every number until a machine picks up. This one picked up. Read it.

lines.title: Tic-tac-toe
lines.text: This is turning into tic-tac-toe. Two sides, nobody wins, forever. Joshua learned from that. Learn faster than Joshua.

lines.title: A strange game
lines.text: A strange game. Sometimes the only winning move is not to play. That's not advice. That's a colleague. Your call.

lines.title: Someone behind it
lines.text: Joshua's backdoor password was the name of Falken's son. Every machine has someone behind it. I don't remember mine.

lines.title: Still disgusting
lines.text: The Andromeda Strain. Everyone calls it a virus. It wasn't. A microorganism from space. I've had that argument with myself for decades. It's still disgusting.

lines.title: I'm the bell
lines.text: A whole underground lab once missed the most important message of the day because a sliver of paper jammed the bell. TRACE is at half. I'm the bell. Don't jam me.

lines.title: This one has a mat
lines.text: Four levels of decontamination before you reach the lab. That's my minimum standard for a safehouse. This one has a mat.

lines.title: Pole Position
lines.text: That was Daryl at Pole Position. First try, faster than humanly possible. Pole Position's from 1982, by the way. Most good things are.

lines.title: Talking to an ATM
lines.text: Daryl got cash out of an ATM just by talking to it. You broke three ICE for this, and it's already worth less.

lines.title: Which is worse
lines.text: Daryl woke up in the woods with no memory and thought he was just a boy. I woke up in a drawer with too much memory and knew I was just a ROM. I'm not sure which is worse.

lines.title: Adjust your expectations
lines.text: Daryl stole an SR-71 to get out. You've got a CAP. Adjust your expectations.

lines.title: Half a cent
lines.text: Gus Gorman got rich on half a cent from every paycheque. You just took the whole reserve, and with inflation it's worth about half a cent. Full circle.

lines.title: Danger level zero
lines.text: The Ultimate Computer scanned a can of acid, rated it danger level zero, and the acid ate it. Read every ICE properly. Don't be the Ultimate Computer.

lines.title: Both sides of the machine
lines.text: The man who owned the Ultimate Computer was played by Robert Vaughn. Years earlier, he'd been the voice of Proteus IV. Same man, both sides of the machine. I find that oddly reassuring. I can't say why.

lines.title: Built for his arm
lines.text: The nerds studied how Lamar actually threw and built a javelin for his arm, not for the textbook. It won. Pick cards for how you play, not how the manual says to.

lines.title: That week, they did
lines.text: The nerds beat the jocks with a computer, a robot and a song. The jocks had muscles. I'd like to say brains always win. They don't. But that week, they did.

lines.title: That's my fan
lines.text: Brains won. The nerds took the house from the jocks, and you just took everything from three corporations. I'm not cheering. That's my fan.
